gui.mcstock.help.1: [What is this] Recycle items into coins, take those coins into a market that ticks every 2 seconds, then spend what you make back on supplies.
gui.mcstock.help.10: [Market events] Each stock has a ~0.25% chance per tick of an event (about once every 13 minutes; doubled in turbulent spells). Events are named and have a life cycle: a sharp move first, then digested with a 20~60 tick (40~120 s) half-life while that stock's volatility runs 1.5~3x.
gui.mcstock.help.11: [Market climate] The three stocks form the equal-weighted Market Index (1000 = all three at base price), shown under the cards on the left. The climate shifts between Calm / Mild / Choppy / Turbulent, 1~10 minutes each; volatility differs between them (candles get fatter and liquidations get closer in turbulent spells).
gui.mcstock.help.12: [News & rumours] The yellow ticker to the right of the chart header is the latest news, a new one every 25 s. Anything tagged as a rumour may well be false and can be clarified later - news is just news, read the chart and judge for yourself.
gui.mcstock.help.13: [Rhythm] A tick every 2 seconds; one candle = 5 ticks = 10s. Red up / green down (Chinese convention). The right-hand scale is the current range; the red dashed line is liquidation.
gui.mcstock.help.14: [Shop] Unit price = value x 1.18, so buy-then-sell loses 18%. Left-click buys 1, Shift+left-click buys a stack; purchases go straight to your bag.
gui.mcstock.help.15: [Conditional orders] The Orders button in the title bar lets you place an order that buys, shorts or closes all when the price rises or falls to a trigger. Checked only on a price tick; fires once at the live price, then is removed. Up to 8 at a time; use the row button to cancel. /mcstock cond also lists and places them.
gui.mcstock.help.2: [Getting started] Craft the Exchange Terminal (or /give @s mcstock:stock_terminal), hold it and right-click to open. The first join grants 1000 coins.
gui.mcstock.help.3: [Recycle] Shift-click inventory items into the recycle bar, then hit Recycle once. Only what is in the bar gets sold - your bag is untouched; used tools, weapons and armor cannot be recycled (brand-new ones can); while in debt the system will not auto-sell any gear that has durability; worthless items are never swallowed (they stay in the bar).
gui.mcstock.help.4: [Market] Qty = shares per buy/sell (1~100000; MAX = the largest order your cash and leverage allow). Leverage 1~400: higher means less margin but a closer liquidation.
gui.mcstock.help.5: [Direction] BUY opens a long, SELL opens a short; they do NOT offset each other. Every position is listed, and the row button closes just that one.
gui.mcstock.help.6: [Money] margin = shares x price / leverage; fee = notional x 0.20%, charged once on open and once on close (0.40% round trip).
gui.mcstock.help.7: [Liquidation & debt] Forced close once the floating loss reaches 45% of the margin: at x2 the liquidation line is 22.5% away, at x400 only 0.11%. Settlement uses the real post-tick price, and you CAN lose through the margin - cash may go negative (debt), with no limit.
gui.mcstock.help.8: [Risk] Markets fall as well as rise, and high leverage is how accounts die. These coins are just game items - don't stake everything on one position.
gui.mcstock.help.9: [Market events] Each stock has a ~0.25% chance per tick of an event (about once every 13 minutes; doubled in turbulent spells). Events are named and have a life cycle: a sharp move first, then digested with a 20~60 tick (40~120 s) half-life while that stock's volatility runs 1.5~3x. Now and then a single-tick 'market move' (about 0.05% per tick) drops the price and only partly recovers - high leverage is what dies there.
